title: Uniform Inference for Sharp Average Marginal Effect Bounds in Fixed-Effects Logit across Hankel Ranks
banked_reason: Cold tier: incremental, paper-score ceiling 5.8 below field threshold 7.4; exact positive-radius marginal minimax values and unrestricted whole-set attainment remain unresolved.
gap_reasons: The recorded topic promises a uniformly honest cone/polynomial-certificate procedure and exact bounded-neighborhood one-sided minimax risks with an attaining compromise, but this node explicitly leaves both the unrestricted values V_{-,R}, V_{+,R} and finite-sample uniform attainment open.

The topic also promises the whole-set minimax consequence, whereas the delivered object is only an attained affine upper program and the node expressly leaves unrestricted V_{set,R}, nonlinear comparison, and globally honest attainment unresolved.

The note does not deliver the advertised optimal honest inference through every Hankel-rank transition: it proves exact risks only at the single rank-one base point, while every positive-radius marginal minimax value and its feasible uniform attainment remain open.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the universal M3/M4 Hausdorff tangent/polar atlas, exact legal focal realization and LAN, exact base-point and rank-oracle risks, ambient-class converse bounds, bounded algebraic certificates, projection honesty, and an attained dependence-aware affine joint benchmark. It did not solve the exact finite-positive-radius all-measurable marginal decision problems or unrestricted whole-set minimax problem, nor construct a separation-free root-n contact-adaptive globally honest attaining procedure. The mathematics passed review, but those missing central deliverables capped the honest package at incremental novelty.
tldr: For the focal \(T=3\), \(x=(0,1,2)\), \(\beta^*=\log2\) AME problem, the note separates three scopes.  First, the kernel-compressed tangent and polar formulas hold at every normalized vector in \(M_3\) and \(M_4\), including moving, merging, and endpoint-approaching rank strata.  Second, constructive legality, compact-uniform LAN, projection honesty, and certificate results are confined to the stated compact positive-slope, positive-cell, positive-information focal subclass.  Third, every procedure uniformly honest on a larger published DDL class containing the focal subexperiment inherits the local Gaussian one-sided lower risks by a direct local-asymptotic testing argument, without any convergence assumption on its decisions.  The two displayed positive squares are support-variance gaps; the corresponding endpoint risk penalty is \(s_e-s_{\mathrm{oracle}}\) times \(\Psi\{\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha_e)\}\).  Dependence-aware bivariate-normal calibration has an attained affine optimum and strictly improves every prescribed nondegenerate Bonferroni split.  Unrestricted positive-radius marginal and joint minimax equality, nonlinear improvement, root-\(n\) contact control, and finite-sample attainment remain open.
gap: DDL identifies the exact sharp closure but leaves uniform sharp-bound coverage open. Pakel--Weidner provides computational outer-bound intervals, not the exact sharp DDL closure, and neither that paper nor generic constrained-inference work solves the rank-transition adaptation problem or computes the focal minimax risks.
fill: Prove the focal all-rank cone and certificate theory, transfer it uniformly over a class with common cell and information bounds, solve the exact Gaussian decision problems on \(H_R\), and either attain them with a certified procedure or prove the sharp separation-free obstruction.
